name: PA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: Rabb's large fundraising and outside support edge
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: This Philadelphia-based seat carries a +40 Democratic lean, and the only serious opposition is an independent who has raised about $11,000 with no outside backing. Chris Rabb has outraised him by more than 100-to-1 and enjoys over $1.5 million in outside support, while markets price a Democratic win near certainty.
model.watch: A surprise independent surge or unusual turnout pattern would be the only realistic path to a closer race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Dwight Evans (D) is not on the ballot.
Dennis Mahoney is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
Dwight Evans's retirement leaves this heavily Democratic Philadelphia seat open, but the fundamentals remain overwhelmingly favorable to the party holding it. The district's partisan lean is roughly +40 Democratic, and the general-election field features Chris Rabb, a well-funded Democrat, against independent Dennis Mahoney, who has raised only about $11,000 and has no outside support.

Rabb has raised over $1.3 million and benefits from roughly $1.6 million in outside spending on his behalf, while no meaningful opposition spending has materialized. Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability near 97 percent. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast rests on the district's lean and the lopsided resource gap, pointing to a comfortable Democratic hold.
